task.title: Withdrawing a failed intent from an open detail form discards typed edits and can swallow a concurrent save failure
task.description:
Deferred from the adversarial review of PR #29 (WB-01KZBT3J1AMW4E5F688WPNZGJZ). Both halves need the render restructuring that WB-01KZC3PGA0QCXKDQ936VPM67D5 owns, so patching them inside the queue would be rewritten immediately.

withdrawFailedIntentFromOpenDetail (internal/webui/assets/index.html, the function above ownsDependencyController) calls renderRoute(), which does main.replaceChildren(detail) and rebuilds every control from latestTasks. Anything typed since the form opened is gone. That much is a deliberate trade and is recorded in the design doc: a form that keeps showing a value the server refused is lying about what is saved, which is worse.

The interaction with an in-flight save is the part worth fixing. Scenario: drag a card while publication is inline and slow, so the board intent is still pending; click into the task; edit the title; hit Save. While that PATCH is open the board intent fails. The withdrawal re-renders and detaches section. The PATCH then also fails, hits 'if (main.firstElementChild !== section) return;' in the detail form's submit catch, and is swallowed with no report at all. The only message on screen is the withdrawal's 'the change made on the board was not applied', which tells the user their board change failed and says nothing about the form save they just made - whose edits are also gone.

What good looks like: the withdrawal corrects only the projected fields and leaves the user's typed edits standing, and a save that is detached mid-flight still reports its outcome somewhere the user will see it. Both fall out naturally once the detail route can be updated in place rather than rebuilt.

Recorded in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-optimistic-web-mutation-queue-design.md under 'A failure with the detail form open'.
